blocks.text: First Samuel 13 records a critical moment in Saul's reign. When Jonathan strikes the Philistine garrison at Geba, the Philistines mobilize in overwhelming response. Israel gathers at Gilgal to resist, but under military pressure and with Samuel's delayed arrival, Saul makes a fateful decision: he performs the burnt offering himself, an act that violates proper religious authority. This transgression marks the beginning of Saul's rejection from enduring kingship.
